summary: Extends issue #200: re-encoded all 164 receipt-backed already-shipped src/L5R.Client/Content/Published/*.jpg files from their WebP working copies (~60% smaller on average), per the user's explicit follow-up request to replace all shipped card images, not just the local dev cache. New tools/content/reencode_published_from_webp.py walks every content/published/*-sources.json manifest, finds each entry's receipt by its recorded image_path, and re-encodes to JPEG only when that receipt has a working_copy, updating the manifest's own image_path/image_sha256 to match. 164 of 181 shipped images qualified; 17 legacy lion-crane-v1 images (predating the images/receipts split) have no receipt and are left untouched. Fixed a real bug caught while writing tests: receipt_path_for only recognized an images/ path segment, so a second run after a first successful migration (image_path now pointing at webp/) could no longer find the receipt at all -- fixed to recognize either.
validation: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/content -> 121/121 (5 new tests in test_reencode_published_from_webp.py: replace-when-working-copy-exists, leave-untouched-when-absent, dry-run, idempotent-rerun-regression, legacy-path-returns-None). Verified all 181 Content/Published/*.jpg (164 replaced + 17 untouched) are still valid, correctly-sized JPEGs via PIL after the migration. No C# touched.
remaining: None; ready for review. The 467 catalogue-wide receipts with no WebP counterpart (from the earlier half of this issue) are unaffected -- none of them are currently shipped published cards.
